# The Milky Way and the God Who Numbers the Stars

## Scripture
*"He determines the number of the stars and calls them each by name. Great is our Lord and mighty in power; his understanding has no limit."* — Psalm 147:4-5 (NIV)

## Reflection
On a clear autumn night, far from city lights, the Milky Way arcs overhead—a river of light made of billions of stars we can barely distinguish. What appears as a faint mist is actually a galaxy so vast that our sun is just one ordinary star among countless billions. It's humbling to realize how small we are within it.

Yet here is the astonishing truth: the God who spoke this galaxy into being also knows you completely. He doesn't just know the number of stars—He calls each by name. Not a single one slips His attention. And if He tends to the vastness of the cosmos with such intimate care, how much more does He hold the details of your life?

When you feel overlooked or insignificant, remember that you are known by the One whose understanding has no limit. The God of the Milky Way is not distant or distracted. He is near, attentive, and mighty to save. Your name is on His heart.

## Prayer
Lord of the stars, You spoke the galaxies into being and call each star by name. Forgive us for doubting that You see us. Thank You that the God of all creation knows us intimately and cares for us deeply. When we feel small, remind us that we are held by infinite love. In Jesus' name, amen.
